title: Review of c06's hidden cost: absolute within-cell decline replicates on fresh seed 5, also at cy=0, where the population instead grows into a few giant cells
summary: Ran c06's abslife.py on three fresh seed-5 genealogies (T=100000): the claim world (cy=0.03, muy 0.02; from 20261025T0935-c07-review-pcell-contained), the low-mutation world (from 20261025T1109-c07-review-somatic-decline) and a new cy=0 run of the claim world (c06's genealogy.py, plus a labkit pack via world_cy0.py, which only sets cy=0). Dying mature cells, yield at birth -> death vs the population mean: cy 0.03: 0.93 -> 0.705 (population 0.972 -> 0.973), 87% declined, n=39; low mutation: 0.884 -> 0.676 (0.971 -> 0.939), 73%, n=11; cy 0: 1.02 -> 0.948 while the population rose 1.054 -> 1.144, 75% declined, n=32. The finding replicates. The cy=0 particles sheet adds context: as mean yield rises the cells grow into a few giant bodies that cover most of the domain (5 cells at t=100000).

observations.H: data/abslife_s5.txt: dying cells decline in absolute yield at cy 0.03 (0.93 -> 0.705), low mutation (0.884 -> 0.676) and cy 0 (1.02 -> 0.948 against a rising population 1.054 -> 1.144)

controls_run.H: population mean yield at the same times (abslife_s5.txt); cy=0 arm (data/gen_cy0_s5.json.gz, rerun_cy0/)

verdicts.limitation: The 'hidden local cost' mechanism is c06's hypothesis and not ablated here either. At cy=0 the world changes regime: rising yield makes cells huge and few (5 at the end, most of the domain inside cells), so it is not a population of small discrete cells like the cy=0.03 world. Dying-cell counts are moderate (11-39) on one seed per regime.
